sentences.text: Russia's president can legally rule until 2036.
Who can vote? Every citizen from 18, also from abroad. Not prisoners, and voting is optional.
For parliament, you get two ballots: one with parties, one with local candidates. Tick one box on each.
Half of the 450 seats go to parties above 5%. The other half go to district winners.
That's the State Duma, which makes the laws. The Federation Council must approve them, but nobody elects it: regions send two each, the president adds up to 30.
The president is elected for six years, with a run-off if no one gets half. He picks the prime minister; the Duma approves. In 2020, Putin's terms were reset to zero.
In 2024, Putin won with 87%. In 2026, United Russia took 349 of 450 seats, with the main liberal party barred.
So, can an election be fair if you already know who'll win?
